newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela inflation to rise after March -Matos.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela inflation to rise after March -Matos.

text.p: Venezuelan monthly inflation will be flat in March after February's 2.3 percent rate, but "it will be very difficult to keep it falling after that", Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
Since Venezuela implemented a tough package of reforms in April last year, monthly inflation has trended downwards from May's 15.6 peak falling to 2.6 percent in January.

But Matos said the trend would reverse after March, as "there'll be an injection of liquidity with the wage increase." Venezuela approved a 75 percent average pay increase in February for its 1.2 million public sector workers
"Monetary policy may have to tighten ... and we'll see that after Congress approves the Central Bank bonds next week," Matos told reporters after a presentation at the Senate Finance Commission.

Matos was referring to the government's $4 billion mega-bond, due to be paid to the Central Bank to cover past government debt. Interest payments on the bond will be serviced by Treasury bills, sold into the market alongside Central Bank TEMs, and used to drain excess liquidity.

Asked if the visiting IMF mission had expressed concern over the fiscal impact of wage increase, Matos said: "the Venezuelan Agenda package of reforms responds to the situation in the country and they (the IMF) recognize that."
